newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. brokerage, exec ordered to pay $4.3 mln.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. brokerage, exec ordered to pay $4.3 mln.

text.p: A former principal of a New York brokerage and the company agreed to pay $4.2 million as restitution for stock manipulation and other violations, the National Association of Securities Dealers' regulatory arm said Tuesday.
Lowell Schatzer, the former principal, also agreed to pay a fine of $120,000 and be barred from the securities industry in any capacity, NASD Regulation said.
The order against Schatzer and his firm, Hanover Sterling & Co Ltd, was part of a settlement of a complaint that the self-regulatory organization initiated in 1995.
An NASD Regulation spokesman described the now-defunct Hanover Sterling as a "bucket shop," a brokerage that accepts orders, but often delays or neglects to fill them out.
Collection of the fine against Lowell was suspended, but would be pursued if Lowell became employed with an NASD-member firm, the spokesman said.

Two others charged in the case, New York brokers Robert Catoggio and Ronan Garber, agreed to settle with the NASD unit by agreeing to pay fines of $50,000 and $120,000, respectively. Both also agreed to be barred from the securities industry.
